newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SML says tug investment tops S$30 mln.
newsitem.headline: SML says tug investment tops S$30 mln.

text.p: The shipping company Sembawang Maritime Ltd (SML) said on Monday it was investing more than Singapore $30 million in six new high performance Z-drive harbour tugs from Japan.
"The acquisition of the new vessels is in line with our fleet upgrading programme to support SML's regional expansion plan," company president Billy Lee said in a statement.
The statement said the new vessels would be fitted with advanced 360-degree steerable rudder propellers to help precise positioning in congested harbour waters.
SML said it had already taken delivery of three 3,200 bhp tugs during 1996, two built by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd in Kobe and one by Matsuura Tekko Zosen Co Ltd in Hiroshima.
SML said it had placed the order for the fourth unit with Matsuura Tekko Zosen and was expecting delivery by June 1997.
The order for the remaining two tugs was expected to be made during the first quarter of 1997, the SML statement said.
